finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.trigger: current_brightness + BRIGHTNESS_INCREMENT or current_brightness - BRIGHTNESS_INCREMENT results in an integer overflow
finding.assumptions: The calculation of new_brightness can overflow if current_brightness is near MAX_BRIGHTNESS or MIN_BRIGHTNESS respectively, and the system does not handle integer overflow gracefully.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Checked clamping logic: lines 67-71 ensure that after any potential overflow, new_brightness is forced into the safe range [MIN_BRIGHTNESS, MAX_BRIGHTNESS]. 2) Verified that BRIGHTNESS_INCREMENT is a compile‑time constant, so no unchecked user input influences the arithmetic. 3) Confirmed that no unchecked signed overflow can bypass the clamping because the subsequent comparison and assignment will correct any wrapped value.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: argv[1] is attacker-controlled and can be crafted to inject malicious commands
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate argv[1] before using it in printf, which could lead to command injection if the output is used in a shell context.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Verified that all printf calls use a compile‑time constant format string. The user input argv[1] is passed only as a %s argument (lines 56, 59, 60, 61), so it cannot influence the format string or cause shell execution. No system, exec, or other command‑invoking functions are called with argv[1]. Therefore there is no OS command injection path.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: brightness is attacker-controlled and can be crafted to inject malicious commands
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate brightness before using it in fprintf, which could lead to command injection if the output is used in a shell context.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any path that would allow user-controlled data to reach a command-executing function. The sink is fprintf to a file, not a shell. Confirmed that brightness is an integer clamped between MIN_BRIGHTNESS and MAX_BRIGHTNESS (lines 67‑71). No format string vulnerability or exec call present. The brightness value is written as plain text; even if attacker can influence it, it cannot inject shell commands.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: file_path is attacker-controlled and can be crafted to inject malicious commands
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate file_path before using it in fopen, which could lead to command injection if the output is used in a shell context.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The only source of the file path is the hard‑coded macro FILE_PATH defined on line 6.  The code never accepts a file path from user input, environment, or other untrusted source.  The calls to fopen in read_brightness (line 23) and write_brightness (line 38) are therefore passing a constant string, not attacker‑controlled data.  Additionally, fopen does not invoke a shell; it simply opens a file, so even if a path were tampered with it would not result in command execution.  There is no code path that could transform untrusted input into a command line that the OS would execute.
